title: MMS convergence study (every element × constitutive model)
objective: Phase 10, step 1: run a method-of-manufactured-solutions convergence study for every supported (element type × constitutive model) combination. Confirm the L2 and H1 error norms converge at the theoretical rate for each combination.
scope: Extend the existing MMS test suite (Plan A P2-T2) to parametrise over all Phase 5 element types and all Phase 3/4/6 constitutive models.
Per combination, run 4 uniformly-refined meshes and fit the log-log slope of the L2 and H1 norms.
Assert the fitted slope matches theory within 0.1 (e.g. linear Hex8 should give L2 slope ~ 2.0, quadratic Hex20 slope ~ 3.0).
Mark as slow (Newton solves on 4 mesh levels).
implementation_steps: Build a parametrised matrix of (element, material, manufactured solution).
Per combination, run the refinement study and fit the convergence rate.
Assertions per combination with documented expected rates.
acceptance_criteria: Every element × material combination converges at the theoretical rate within 0.1.
Test suite runs as part of the `slow` tier.
risks: Some combinations have NO closed-form manufactured solution. Mitigation: restrict MMS to elastic combinations and use engineering benchmarks for dissipative models.
implementation_branch: ph10_preq (work/phase10-e6-generalized-mms) merged to main via PR #122
completion_notes: Delivered via ph10_preq sub-plan Phase 6 (E6 Generalized MMS). PLAN-B closure 2026-04-26 on SOSOVSKI/plan-b-ph10-exec.
Matrix covers Hex8/Tet10/Hex20 × SVK plus Hex8 × {J2/Perzyna/Lemaitre} via documented elastic_regime_interpolation policy for dissipative materials (per task risk note).
Fitted L2/H1 slopes asserted within entry-specific tolerance (default 0.1).
